notes: Each "props" object has all 43 tree_props fields, named and ordered exactly as the C++ struct in tree_system.cpp (and TREE_PROP_NAMES in tests.js), so it can be assigned straight onto the tree props object: for (k in props) tree[k] = props[k]; tree.needs_update = true.

Units: 1 unit ~ 1 m. The coast redwood is scaled down, and all values stay inside the tests.js slider ranges. The stored seed is a typical-looking one; other seeds give natural variation (see generated.height_over_seeds_1_to_12) because lengthJitter, radiusJitter, azimuthJitter and elevationJitter are non-zero.

leaf_texture is the id of the twig card texture and twig is its full definition, painted by engine.vegi_textures.leaf (vegi_textures.js): kind = leaf shape (ovate oblong round heart narrow scale lobed maple fan palmate compound; needle feather frond; blossom), color = base leaf rgb, count = leaves per card, size = leaf length as a fraction of the card, spread = radius of the leaf cloud as a fraction of the card, hang = 0 leaves point outwards / 1 they hang down, stem = rgb of the twig itself; compound also has leaflets (pairs) and lw (leaflet width / length), blossom has eye (flower centre rgb) and leaf_color. Load every definition with engine.vegi_textures.leaf.register_presets(json), then engine.vegi_textures.leaf.pixels(leaf_texture, size) gives { width, height, data }. Twig cards are alpha-cut leaf textures and tree_generate colours them with the bark colour, so draw them with a material that does not use vertex colour. Requires the 43-prop tree_system.cpp (the last six fields are the jitter props, twigCards and twigNormalBlend). twigCards and twigNormalBlend give foliage volume (crossed cards, normals leaning out of the crown); set them to 1 and 0 for the old flat cards. All the *Jitter props can be set to 0 for the old, regular branching.

bark: { style, scale, seed } picks a procedural bark texture + normal map (bark_textures.js, style names in bark_textures.STYLES). scale = how many texture tiles repeat across half the trunk circumference; the bark colour comes from the barkColor props (vertex colour), which multiplies the texture. The trunk UVs run u round the trunk (mirrored) and v along it in units of (radius / maxRadius) / vMultiplier, so a material scales uv by (scale, scale / (pi * maxRadius * vMultiplier)) to keep the texels square; see make_bark_material in tests.js.

trees.name: English oak
trees.description: Massive short bole with strong buttress flare, forking low into a very broad, spreading crown of thick limbs.

trees.name: Scots pine
trees.description: Tall, straight, slender, reddish-brown trunk with a long clear bole and a small crown at the top.

trees.name: Silver birch
trees.description: Slender, slightly meandering white trunk with fine ascending limbs.

trees.name: Italian cypress
trees.description: Narrow columnar tree: dead-straight trunk with short limbs held tight against the stem.

trees.name: Coast redwood
trees.description: Very tall, straight, strongly tapering red-brown trunk with a buttressed base and short limbs. Scaled down: real trees reach 60-90 m.

trees.name: Baobab
trees.description: Enormous squat swollen trunk topped by a few short, very thick limbs.

trees.name: Weeping willow
trees.description: Short thick trunk forking low into arching limbs that droop at the tips (negative dropAmount, positive growAmount).

trees.name: Olive
trees.description: Short, gnarled, twisting trunk with strong meander and wide-spreading limbs.

trees.name: Sugar maple
trees.description: Straight, clean bole with ascending limbs forming a rounded crown.

trees.name: Quaking aspen
trees.description: Tall, very slender, pale greenish-white straight trunk with a small high crown.

trees.name: Common beech
trees.description: Smooth grey trunk with strong flare, forking into a dense, broad, rounded crown.

trees.name: Norway spruce
trees.description: Straight conical tree with one leader and many short, slightly drooping limbs. Scaled down: real trees reach 35-50 m.

trees.name: Lombardy poplar
trees.description: Narrow fastigiate column of tightly upswept limbs.

trees.name: Umbrella thorn acacia
trees.description: Short forking trunk carrying a wide, spreading, flat-topped crown.

trees.name: Coconut palm
trees.description: Tall slender unbranched trunk with a crown of large arching fronds at the top. An approximation: the generator has no true palm, so this is a long bare trunk whose last forks carry big frond cards. Shortened: real trees reach 20-30 m.

trees.name: Cherry blossom
trees.description: Short trunk dividing into spreading limbs under a dense cloud of pink blossom.

trees.name: Blue gum eucalyptus
trees.description: Very tall straight pale trunk with a sparse high crown of drooping foliage. Scaled down: real trees reach 40-55 m.

trees.name: Cedar of Lebanon
trees.description: Massive short trunk with wide, tiered, near-horizontal limbs.

trees.name: Ginkgo
trees.description: Straight upright trunk with irregular ascending limbs and fan-shaped leaves.

trees.name: London plane
trees.description: Tall pale mottled trunk forking into large spreading limbs.

trees.name: Japanese maple
trees.description: Small low-branching ornamental forming a dome of red palmate foliage.

trees.name: Stone pine
trees.description: Long clear reddish trunk topped by a broad umbrella crown.

trees.name: Southern live oak
trees.description: Short massive trunk with huge, wide-spreading, near-horizontal limbs and small evergreen leaves.

trees.name: European larch
trees.description: Straight slender trunk with whorled limbs and light tufts of needles. Scaled down: real trees reach 25-40 m.

trees.name: White ash
trees.description: Straight, clean bole with open ascending limbs; diamond-patterned ridged bark and compound leaves.

trees.name: Black walnut
trees.description: Tall straight trunk with very dark, deeply furrowed bark and a broad open crown of large compound leaves.

trees.name: Horse chestnut
trees.description: Stout trunk and a dense domed crown whose lower limbs sweep down; large palmate leaves.

trees.name: Sweet chestnut
trees.description: Massive, often leaning trunk with bark ridges that spiral round it; heavy spreading limbs.

trees.name: Field elm
trees.description: Upright trunk dividing into a vase-shaped crown of arching limbs; deeply fissured bark.

trees.name: Small-leaved lime
trees.description: Straight trunk and a dense, rounded crown of small heart-shaped leaves.

trees.name: Douglas fir
trees.description: Very tall conical conifer with a corky, deeply furrowed trunk and irregular, slightly drooping limbs. Scaled down: real trees reach 50-80 m.

trees.name: Western red cedar
trees.description: Buttressed, fibrous-barked trunk with drooping, upturned-tipped sprays in a narrow cone. Scaled down: real trees reach 40-60 m.

trees.name: Giant sequoia
trees.description: Colossal, fluted, fibrous red trunk with a swollen buttressed base and short, high limbs. Scaled down: real trees reach 70-95 m.

trees.name: Ponderosa pine
trees.description: Tall, long-boled pine with orange, jigsaw-plated bark and long needles in tufts. Scaled down: real trees reach 40-70 m.

trees.name: Black locust
trees.description: Crooked, irregularly branched tree with very deep, twisting ridges and light compound leaves.

trees.name: Cork oak
trees.description: Short, thick, gnarled trunk wrapped in thick, knobbly cork; wide evergreen crown.

trees.name: Jacaranda
trees.description: Spreading, vase-shaped crown that carries a haze of lilac-blue trumpet flowers.

trees.name: Date palm
trees.description: Thick, straight trunk patterned with old leaf bases, topped by a crown of stiff grey-green fronds. An approximation like the coconut palm.

trees.name: Bald cypress
trees.description: Strongly flared, fibrous-barked trunk, conical crown of feathery, light-green deciduous sprays.

trees.name: Snow gum
trees.description: Short, crooked multi-limbed gum with smooth cream-and-grey patchwork bark and drooping grey-green leaves.
